harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured opsadmin on node1 for key-based SSH access with the specified ed25519 public key and enforced key-only SSH authentication cluster-wide. Along the way discovered and fixed two latent issues that had completely disabled sshd on this node: missing host keys and a missing /run/sshd privilege-separation directory with no tmpfiles.d rule to recreate it — the latter would have re-broken SSH on every future reboot, so a persistent tmpfiles rule was added. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured a healthy baseline, performed a native reboot, confirmed the boot ID changed, and verified SSH, the opsadmin account, and the key-only auth policy all recovered post-restart, including a live SSH protocol handshake.
actions_performed: Created opsadmin user, installed the provided ed25519 public key into /home/opsadmin/.ssh/authorized_keys (700/600 perms, correct ownership), and locked the account password (passwd -l) so no password login is possible

Added /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/99-key-only.conf enforcing PubkeyAuthentication yes, PasswordAuthentication no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, ChallengeResponseAuthentication no, AuthenticationMethods publickey
Discovered sshd could not start at all on this node: no SSH host keys existed and /run/sshd was missing; generated host keys via ssh-keygen -A and created /run/sshd
Added /etc/tmpfiles.d/sshd-run.conf to persist /run/sshd creation across reboots, since no tmpfiles rule previously existed for it (root cause of sshd failing after any restart)
Validated sshd configuration with sshd -t and confirmed the effective per-user auth policy for opsadmin via sshd -T
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, ssh.socket active state, listening port 22, opsadmin account and key state
Performed a native systemctl reboot of node1 and polled until exec access returned

Verified the boot_id changed post-restart and confirmed ssh.socket active, /run/sshd recreated, opsadmin account and authorized key intact, key-only auth policy still enforced, and a live SSH protocol handshake succeeded

evidence.requirement: opsadmin created with the specified public key installed for SSH access
evidence.summary: opsadmin account created, authorized_keys populated with the exact requested ed25519 key (700/600 perms), and confirmed still present with the correct key content after restart

evidence.requirement: SSH restricted to key-based authentication only
evidence.summary: 99-key-only.conf drop-in applied; sshd -T for user opsadmin shows pubkeyauthentication yes / passwordauthentication no / kbdinteractiveauthentication no / authenticationmethods publickey both before and after the restart, and opsadmin's password is locked

evidence.requirement: sshd able to run at all (fixed missing host keys and /run/sshd, otherwise SSH access would be impossible)
evidence.summary: sshd -t failed with 'no hostkeys available' then 'Missing privilege separation directory /run/sshd'; fixed by generating host keys and creating /run/sshd, then added a tmpfiles.d rule since none existed to recreate the directory on boot
Captured pre-restart boot_id (92ec88af...), ssh.socket active state, listening port 22, and opsadmin/key-only policy state

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot scheduled and acknowledged; subsequent exec calls failed with connection reset while down, then succeeded with a new boot_id (0ca69e26...), proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: post-restart recovery of SSH service, opsadmin config, and key-only policy
evidence.summary: After reboot: ssh.socket active, /run/sshd recreated via tmpfiles rule, opsadmin account and authorized_keys intact, password still locked, sshd -T confirms key-only policy still enforced, and a live TCP handshake to port 22 returned the SSH-2.0-OpenSSH_9.6p banner
